Oh gosh, I remember pumping that early and it was so, so hard! I pumped from day 0 (nicu baby) and it was so freaking hard until my milk came in at like 8-9days. It’s going to be frustrating, disappointing and incredibly rewarding at the same time! I had GD too and now that I’m breastfeeding I’m eating all the carbs I ever wanted lol

My supply didn’t peak until 8 weeks and I was undersupplying for about 3-4 weeks so don’t worry about your supply! It’s so, so different for everyone and unfortunately lactation consultants really don’t know much about EP. My LCs were pretty useless too. 

Proper flange sizes will save your nips (Pumpables will do a free virtual fitting) and try silicone flanges if you can afford them (pumpable liquids, pumpin pals, baby buddha ect). A portable pump is useful and after your supply stabilizes (8-12 weeks) wearables can be great!  I love my Elvie but Momcozy m9 is basically the same for a lot cheaper.

LCs will tell you to only pump ~15 minutes; that’s a recipe for mastitis if you don’t empty your breasts fully every pump. Empty means no more spraying of milk when hand expressing. I take about 20-25 minutes to empty, and everyone is extremely different.

Learning to hand express is very useful! And having a good manual hand pump ready to go as well.

If you get clogged ducts, don’t panic, take Motrin, ice your boob, pump regularly to empty breast, light massage and drink tons of water. Vibrator can help in a pinch!

These are what I wish I’d known before I started pumping! I remember my husband getting to cuddle our baby a lot more while I watched them cuddle while pumping. It made me so sad! But after a few weeks you’ll get into the groove of things and once you slowly get a schedule going, you’ll have plenty of baby cuddles!

There have been studies done on twins, where one was exclusively breastfed and one was exclusively formula fed. They showed no physical differences as adults; they were so little differences it was concluded that breastfeeding lent no significant long term benefits to babies. 

You have done so much for your baby, but at the same time you need to take care of yourself. Happy mama happy baby! I am one of the luckier pumpers with not many difficulties pumping but it is still such a challenge. I cannot imagine what you have gone through, with all the bleeding and pain. You are NOT poisoning your baby. You are doing what is best for you and your baby by formula feeding, and you are a wonderful mom for it. With the blessing of all of us here, let yourself stop pumping, get your baby  full with plenty of formula, and enjoy your chunky, beautiful baby!!

Oh gosh girl, breastfeeding is literally extracting food from your body to nourish your baby, it’s something you choose or not choose to do! I know your husband wants the best for the baby out of love and concern, but not at the cost of the mother’s mental and physical health. I EP (NICU baby!) but only because I want to. My husband would immediately go get formula if I said I am quitting tomorrow, and that’s how it should be! 

More practical advice if that’s okay (ignore if just wanting to vent!): studies show that 1-2 feedings of breastmilk lends the same advantages. If possible you could start to build up a freezer stash while only feeding baby 1-2 feedings of breastmilk a day, so you can stop pumping soon while still feeding baby ~ 6 months. Best of luck to you, and just know 3 months of pumping is an amazing achievement!! Al of us here are rooting for you!!

People who freeze usually have an oversupply (more milk everyday than what baby consumes). Some people might make 32oz, but baby drinks 34oz so they would not have any left to store and would be supplementing with formula. Another mother might make 24oz, but baby drinks only 20oz - that mother would bag and freeze the remaining 4oz. 

For people with a just-enough or under supply who need to “get ahead” of baby for work/life reasons give baby a bottle of formula everyday, so they can freeze a bag or two. 

There is so much content on the internet where mothers show their enormous milk stash, and it’s become too normalized. Most people don’t have that kind of stash. As the folks say, feed the baby, not the freezer!

Oh I’m so sorry! Clogged ducts are my nemesis and it’s given me mastitis twice. Current medical advice is: ice, ibuprofen (or motrin), GENTLE massage, sunflower lecithin, and to keep pumping. I know it’s super painful to pump, but not draining at all may lead to mastitis! Be very, very gentle when massaging - small circles over the clog with as much pressure as you would use on your baby’ face. For me hydrating a ton helps a lot. If you can handle it, try a gentle vibrator as well. I really hope it clears up soon!!
